items.title: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.excerpt: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.

items.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan to put AI data centers in space
items.excerpt: The FCC dismissed some of the key concerns raised by opponents, including potential threats to scientific research, because the agency determined they fell outside its regulatory authority.

items.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
items.excerpt: OpenAI will introduce a single usage meter across ChatGPT as it combines the Chat and Work experiences.

items.title: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.excerpt: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.

items.title: The canceled Tesla Cybertruck is the fastest-selling used truck in America
items.excerpt: The Tesla Cybertruck was the fastest-selling used truck last month, averaging just 39.1 days on the market compared to 65.5 days for trucks overall.

items.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
items.excerpt: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushes back against rivals’ accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading AI companies increasingly automate their own research and model development.

items.title: 1Password said hackers broke into its internal systems, but customer passwords are safe
items.excerpt: The password manager maker said an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate account and took some information about customers.

items.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
items.excerpt: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.

items.title: DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers
items.excerpt: U.S. prosecutors accused the former executive of defrauding victims of ransomware by paying the hackers, charging victims more, and pocketing the difference.

items.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
items.excerpt: The proposed Character.ai bankruptcy sale includes sensitive personal data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors, the state AGs said.

items.title: X’s latest update for creators focuses on vertical video
items.excerpt: As short-form video ramps up in popularity, X's new creation tools are part of its effort to compete with YouTube and Instagram.

items.title: WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages in group and individual chats
items.excerpt: Users can schedule messages from 10 minutes later to after 14 days.

items.title: Allstate suffers multiday tech outage ahead of Thanksgiving
items.excerpt: The disruption comes at a particularly bad time for the insurance giant, as millions of Americans prepare to travel for the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.

items.title: Todoist confirms 6% of customers’ details were stolen in data breach
items.excerpt: Todoist said a hacker gained access to its production systems and stole customer data, including email IDs, password hashes, and account creation dates.

items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
items.excerpt: Amazon and Meta are discussing a potential deal that would end a two-month-long blockade of Muse.

items.title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to step down next week amid IPO uncertainty
items.excerpt: Flipkart's product and technology chief Balaji Thiagarajan will lead the company alongside its board until a successor is found.

items.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
items.excerpt: The central question for investigators is what Nvidia knew about where those chips ended up and whether Huang's affair with a Megaspeed executive gave the company reason to doubt Megaspeed's assurances.

items.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
items.excerpt: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the

items.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’
items.excerpt: Huang faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.

items.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
items.excerpt: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.
